summary: Issue 4 — Temporary Material. Page 1: Delayed Part. The replacement-bracket problem begins as an ordinary maintenance problem, not a material discovery.

panelPlan.text: PANEL 1 — Maintenance bay. A coolant-balancing unit is open in the wall. A red strip reads: TEMPORARY FLOW INSTABILITY — NON-CATASTROPHIC BUT ANNOYING.
PANEL 2 — Zib studies a cracked stabilizer bracket. ZIB: Of course.
PANEL 3 — Astra enters with coffee and three unrelated forms. ASTRA: Tell me this is normal annoying.
PANEL 4 — Zib points into the housing. ZIB: Stabilizer bracket.
PANEL 5 — Procurement display: REPLACEMENT PART ETA: 19 DAYS. ZIB: Counterpoint.

summary: Page 2: Nineteen Days. Astra assigns Jax the concrete monitoring job while temporary-repair bureaucracy arrives.

panelPlan.text: PANEL 1 — Astra reads the ETA twice. ASTRA: Nineteen days for a bracket.
PANEL 2 — Zib keeps working. ZIB: Twelve if someone lies correctly.
PANEL 3 — Astra does not look up. ASTRA: We are not doing procurement fraud before lunch.
PANEL 4 — Jax arrives with a handheld flow reader. JAX: Good. I already had lunch.
PANEL 5 — Astra points at the unit. ASTRA: You are on readings. Jax looks at the reader, then the unit, and accepts that this is now his morning.
PANEL 6 — Pixa projects a form: TEMPORARY MATERIAL USAGE REQUEST — JUSTIFY DEVIATION FROM IDEAL REALITY. PIXA: Temporary repair authorization is available. ASTRA: That title feels personal.

summary: Page 3: One Sample. Mira notices a physical difference between retained residue samples without assigning meaning to it.

panelPlan.text: PANEL 1 — Mira works at a nearby lab bench with sealed samples retained from prior incidents. Labels are physical and cautious, including: PRESSURE CORRELATION — CONTENT UNKNOWN.
PANEL 2 — She presses a brittle fragment with a probe. It crumbles.
PANEL 3 — She taps a denser fragment against a steel test block. It clicks instead of flaking.
PANEL 4 — Mira stops. MIRA: Huh.
PANEL 5 — Zib glances over from the wall. ZIB: Useful huh or dangerous huh.
PANEL 6 — Mira looks at the fragment, genuinely uncertain. MIRA: Not yet either.

summary: Page 4: Control First. The first result is deliberately small: one sample crumbles and one does not.

panelPlan.text: PANEL 1 — Mira repeats the same simple compression test on both samples.
PANEL 2 — She records the result. MIRA: Same residue class. Different post-formation cohesion.
PANEL 3 — Zib stares at her. ZIB: English.
PANEL 4 — Mira holds up the two samples. MIRA: One crumbles. One doesn't.
PANEL 5 — Astra nods. ASTRA: That I can approve.
PANEL 6 — Mira immediately qualifies it. MIRA: I haven't explained why. ASTRA: Even better.

summary: Page 5: Temporary Means Owner. Glorp and Kreeb reduce temporary-repair procedure to owner, expiry, and inspection while Jax takes the readings.

panelPlan.text: PANEL 1 — Glorp reviews the temporary repair authorization with visible alarm.
PANEL 2 — Glorp taps the word TEMPORARY. GLORP: Temporary systems become permanent through exhaustion.
PANEL 3 — Kreeb reads beside them. KREEB: Then label the exhaustion.
PANEL 4 — Zib, from inside the wall compartment: Label the bracket.
PANEL 5 — Glorp reluctantly reduces the procedure to three required fields: OWNER / EXPIRY / INSPECTION INTERVAL.
PANEL 6 — Jax raises the flow reader. JAX: I can take the readings. Astra nods once. No ceremony.

summary: Page 6: Bench Test. Mira and Zib try to make the sample fail safely before allowing it near station infrastructure.

panelPlan.text: PANEL 1 — Mira and Zib build a small off-line test rig. Nothing touches station infrastructure yet.
PANEL 2 — Mira sets the sequence. MIRA: Heat first. Compression second. Then vibration.
PANEL 3 — Zib watches her deliberately abuse the sample. ZIB: You say that like you want it to fail.
PANEL 4 — Mira does not look up. MIRA: I want it to fail here.
PANEL 5 — The fragment survives heat and compression, then chips under sustained vibration.
PANEL 6 — Zib points at the damaged sample. ZIB: So it is not a bracket. MIRA: Correct.

summary: Page 7: First Patch. The residue is used only as gap filler inside a conventional temporary brace; the approved clamp carries the load.

panelPlan.text: PANEL 1 — Zib builds a conventional temporary brace from approved clamp hardware and mesh. The residue fragment is used only as gap-filling material inside the brace.
PANEL 2 — Astra watches closely. ASTRA: Say exactly what it is doing.
PANEL 3 — Zib tightens the approved clamp. ZIB: Filling a gap. Clamp carries the load.
PANEL 4 — Mira checks the configuration. MIRA: That I can defend.
PANEL 5 — The unit restarts. Status changes to: FLOW STABILITY: QUESTIONABLE BUT IMPROVED. ZIB: Don't celebrate questionable.

summary: Page 8: Watch the Number. Jax stays on the boring monitoring task and catches a small shift before it becomes a larger problem.

panelPlan.text: PANEL 1 — Jax watches the handheld reader beside the unit.
PANEL 2 — He logs the first interval. JAX: Flow is holding.
PANEL 3 — Astra checks the temporary tag. ASTRA: Again in ten.
PANEL 4 — Jax shows her the handwritten schedule. JAX: I know. That is why I wrote ten.
PANEL 5 — At the next reading, Jax notices a slight shift before anyone else does. JAX: Right side moved two millimeters.
PANEL 6 — Zib isolates the unit immediately. ZIB: Good catch. JAX: I was hoping you would say "nothing."

summary: Page 9: Second Patch. Zib increases conventional reinforcement and reduces the weird material; Pixa reports only the physical result.

panelPlan.text: PANEL 1 — Zib opens the brace again.
PANEL 2 — He adds more approved mesh and reduces the amount of residue filler. ZIB: More mesh. Less weird.
PANEL 3 — Mira agrees. MIRA: That is also my preferred ratio.
PANEL 4 — Jax holds the reader ready while Astra keeps the temporary authorization visible at the workbench.
PANEL 5 — Zib restarts the unit.
PANEL 6 — Pixa displays only the physical result. PIXA: Flow variance reduced by eighteen percent. ZIB: Worse somehow.

summary: Page 10: It Works At All. The crew permits exactly one conclusion: the filler did not get in the way of a conventional clamp surviving two cycles.

panelPlan.text: PANEL 1 — The unit completes another cycle.
PANEL 2 — Mira checks the patch. MIRA: Two cycles.
PANEL 3 — Zib refuses to over-credit it. ZIB: The clamp survived. The filler did not get in the way.
PANEL 4 — Mira smiles despite herself. MIRA: That is a material result.
PANEL 5 — Astra hears the phrase from across the bay. ASTRA: Nobody says "commercial" until I am dead.
PANEL 6 — Brick, already present, writes in his notebook: THE WEIRD THING GOT A JOB.

summary: Page 11: What We Know. Mira's small results board creates the unavoidable reporting question.

panelPlan.text: PANEL 1 — Mira builds a small results board: heat exposure, compression, vibration damage, installed configuration.
PANEL 2 — She looks at Astra. MIRA: What we know is small.
PANEL 3 — Astra relaxes slightly. ASTRA: I like small.
PANEL 4 — Mira points toward the temporary repair form. MIRA: You will hate the next part.
PANEL 5 — She shows the reporting requirement. MIRA: Safety record requires the material event.
PANEL 6 — Astra closes her eyes. ASTRA: There it is.

summary: Page 12: Report Required. Traceability wins: if the material touched a system, its history has to be accurate.

panelPlan.text: PANEL 1 — Glorp traces the temporary-deviation reporting path on a tablet.
PANEL 2 — Glorp looks up. GLORP: If it touched a system, it has a history.
PANEL 3 — Kreeb answers calmly. KREEB: Then make the history accurate.
PANEL 4 — Astra points at the report destination. ASTRA: Internal?
PANEL 5 — Glorp shakes their head. GLORP: No.
PANEL 6 — Zib shuts the wall panel. ZIB: Nobody made the reporting tree. It grew.

summary: Page 13: The Argument. Mira wants an accurate report; Astra fears one patch will be institutionalized as a discovery.

panelPlan.text: PANEL 1 — Astra and Mira stand across the workbench. Neither is angry. Both understand the stakes.
PANEL 2 — Mira keeps her voice level. MIRA: If this matters, we should report it correctly.
PANEL 3 — Astra answers just as quietly. ASTRA: If this matters, we should survive reporting it.
PANEL 4 — Astra points to the single patched unit. ASTRA: And turning one patch into a discovery is not science.
PANEL 5 — Mira meets her gaze. MIRA: I wasn't going to.

summary: Page 14: The Real Fear. Astra names the institutional chain she fears: anomaly to category to target to budget to production pressure.

panelPlan.text: PANEL 1 — Mira studies Astra instead of the sample. MIRA: What do you think happens?
PANEL 2 — Astra gestures toward the report. ASTRA: A useful anomaly gets a category.
PANEL 3 — She continues. ASTRA: A category gets a target. A target gets a budget.
PANEL 4 — Astra looks around the station. ASTRA: Then the budget tells us how to make more of it.
PANEL 5 — Mira answers the part Astra cannot dismiss. MIRA: The station needs a budget.
PANEL 6 — Astra nods. ASTRA: I know. That's the problem.

summary: Page 15: Stop Arguing Like a Meeting. Zib makes Astra and Mira continue the decision while physically finishing the job.

panelPlan.text: PANEL 1 — Zib, still trying to finish the actual repair, interrupts them. ZIB: Stop arguing like a meeting.
PANEL 2 — Astra turns. ASTRA: We are making a decision.
PANEL 3 — Zib hands Astra part of the brace. ZIB: Then make it while holding this.
PANEL 4 — He gives Mira the sensor lead. The three of them resume work.
PANEL 5 — Mira keeps talking while checking the sensor. MIRA: I can write only what the test supports.
PANEL 6 — Astra holds the brace steady. ASTRA: And what it doesn't. MIRA: Especially that.

summary: Page 16: Bounded Language. The report states the ugly practical use and its limits without turning it into a mechanism.

panelPlan.text: PANEL 1 — Glorp, Kreeb, Mira, and Astra work around one terminal rather than holding another meeting.
PANEL 2 — The report contains the sentence: Incidental residue contributed to temporary gap filling under monitored conditions. Structural load remained on approved clamp. Repeatability unknown.
PANEL 3 — Glorp studies it. GLORP: Ugly can still be auditable.
PANEL 4 — Kreeb nods. KREEB: And honest.
PANEL 5 — Astra reads the sentence again. ASTRA: That is ugly.
PANEL 6 — Mira looks toward the patched unit. MIRA: So was the repair.

summary: Page 17: Signature. Jax completes his monitoring log; Astra signs and sends only the narrow version because there is no defensible broad version.

panelPlan.text: PANEL 1 — Jax arrives with the completed monitoring log.
PANEL 2 — He hands it to Astra. JAX: Four cycles. Still inside temporary limits.
PANEL 3 — Astra checks the intervals. ASTRA: You finished the log.
PANEL 4 — Jax shrugs. JAX: It kept asking for numbers, so I gave it numbers.
PANEL 5 — The report waits on STATION MANAGER SIGNATURE.
PANEL 6 — Astra signs. ASTRA: Send the narrow version. MIRA: There is only a narrow version.

summary: Page 18: Monitor Shift. Jax stays through the next reading because the task is his, not because anyone is watching him do it.

panelPlan.text: PANEL 1 — Later. The maintenance bay is quiet. Jax remains beside the reader for the next scheduled interval.
PANEL 2 — Zib passes through. ZIB: You can go.
PANEL 3 — Jax checks the clock. JAX: I know. The next reading is in six minutes.
PANEL 4 — Zib looks at him, mildly surprised.
PANEL 5 — Jax does not look up. JAX: Don't make it a ceremony.
PANEL 6 — The gauge stays within the temporary band.

summary: Page 19: Send. Astra and Mira remove any language stronger than the evidence before Astra sends the report herself.

panelPlan.text: PANEL 1 — Astra and Mira perform the final read together.
PANEL 2 — Astra points at a modifier. ASTRA: No "stronger."
PANEL 3 — Mira edits it. MIRA: Removed.
PANEL 4 — Astra checks the causal language. ASTRA: No "produced by."
PANEL 5 — Mira does not touch the screen. MIRA: Wasn't there.
PANEL 6 — Astra hits SEND herself. ASTRA: Good.

summary: Page 20: Acknowledged. The bounded report is immediately forwarded to Resource Efficiency Review, proving Astra's fear institutionally rather than scientifically.

panelPlan.text: PANEL 1 — A notification arrives almost immediately: OBSERVATIONAL REPORT RECEIVED.
PANEL 2 — Astra exhales. ASTRA: Good.
PANEL 3 — A second line appears: FORWARDED TO: RESOURCE EFFICIENCY REVIEW.
PANEL 4 — Astra's expression changes. ASTRA: No.
PANEL 5 — Mira reads it. MIRA: That was fast.
PANEL 6 — Brick closes his notebook. BRICK: Appetite found the address.

summary: Page 21: Still Temporary. The repair remains monitored and temporary even as the station receives its first value flag.

panelPlan.text: PANEL 1 — Next cycle. The repaired unit hums. The temporary tag is still prominent: INSPECT / EXPIRES / OWNER.
PANEL 2 — Zib checks procurement. REPLACEMENT PART ETA: 18 DAYS.
PANEL 3 — Astra points at the patch. ASTRA: Still temporary.
PANEL 4 — Zib closes the panel. ZIB: Everything is temporary if procurement is involved.
PANEL 5 — Mira seals another physical sample. MIRA: No new claim.
PANEL 6 — Pixa's screen lights: PRELIMINARY INTEREST FLAGGED. Nobody speaks.

summary: Page 22: Tag — Value Identified. Astra and Mira agree the report was necessary even as commercial-interest machinery arrives immediately.

panelPlan.text: PANEL 1 — Astra's terminal expands the notification: PRELIMINARY COMMERCIAL INTEREST FLAGGED.
PANEL 2 — A smaller line appears beneath it: THANK YOU FOR YOUR CONTRIBUTION TO STATION VALUE IDENTIFICATION.
PANEL 3 — Astra stares at the wording. ASTRA: There it is.
PANEL 4 — Mira remains beside her. MIRA: I still think we had to report it. ASTRA: We did.
PANEL 5 — Astra looks through the glass toward the functioning maintenance bay. ASTRA: I just wanted one more day before it got a department.
